title: 2026 American Geophysical Union Annual Meeting · Events · CUAHSI
description: CUAHSI at the AGU Annual Meeting, December 7 to 11, 2026, in San Francisco. Exhibit booth: CUAHSI is at booth #632; stop by to learn about its services and programs. Community gathering: December 9, 6 to 9 pm PST, at Underdogs Cantina, a chance to connect with CUAHSI staff and water science community members. Town Hall: "CUAHSI Turns 25: Shaping the Future of Water Science Infrastructure and Education," December 9, 1 to 2 pm PST, in MC Room 2007 - West. Sessions co-convened by CUAHSI staff: H014, Advances in Integrated Hydrological Modeling: Methods, Solvers, and Computational Innovation (conveners Nick Engdahl, Danielle Tijerina-Kreuzer and Amelia Peeples); H005, Advanced Capabilities for Hydrology Community Model and Data Infrastructure (David Tarboton, Martyn Clark, Laura Condon and Jordan Read); and H140, Uniting Community Water Resources Modeling and Operational Hydrology (Steven Burian, Martyn Clark, Katie van Werkhoven, Jordan Read and Louise Arnal). Staff presentation times will be announced closer to the meeting.

description: Submission deadline for AGU Fall Meeting 2026 abstracts, including four sessions co-convened by CUAHSI staff on integrated hydrological modeling, community model and data infrastructure, water resources modeling and operational hydrology, and near-surface geophysics field operations standards.

Nominations must be submitted by a faculty member, academic advisor, or research or professional mentor.

Networking is the ultimate catalyst for an early-career researcher. Good for graduate students weighing careers outside the tenure track.

description: Annual CSDMS meeting bringing together researchers in surface dynamics modeling.

title: CUAHSI Community Gathering at AGU 2026 · Events · CUAHSI

CUAHSI also holds a Town Hall earlier the same day. RSVP sign-ups will be announced.

title: CUAHSI Turns 25: Shaping the Future of Water Science Infrastructure and Education · Events · CUAHSI
description: Time: 1 to 2 pm PST (13:00 to 14:00). CUAHSI's Town Hall at the AGU Annual Meeting (December 7 to 11, 2026), session TH33F, in MC Room 2007 - West. Shaping the future of water science infrastructure and education as CUAHSI turns 25.

title: CyberWater2 Training · Events · CUAHSI
description: A hands-on model training program led by the University of Pittsburgh, Indiana University Indianapolis and CUAHSI, scheduled for the week of September 21 to 25, 2026: live virtual sessions on Monday (9/21) and Wednesday (9/23), self-paced exercises with office hours through the week, and a wrap-up on Friday (9/25). Learning objectives: navigate the CyberWater interface and build workflows, run a model simulation, use the components of the generic model agent toolkit for model integration, and use CyberWater to answer new scientific questions. Two tracks were offered: training plus certificate with a $200 stipend for participants at US institutions, and training only. A Windows system was needed for the exercises. Applications closed August 28, 2026. Recordings of some of the sessions are in the cyberseminar archive.

title: Data Publishing Program · Events · CUAHSI
description: A three-week virtual cohort program that helps researchers clear the last mile of data publishing, with step-by-step training on preparing and publishing scientific data in HydroShare. For researchers with datasets near or ready for publication who can attend most or all sessions. Registration closed October 2, 2026.

title: Webinar Series: Integrating Hydrology and Geophysics · Events · CUAHSI
description: Joint series with the EarthScope-operated NSF National Geophysical Facility. Four sessions at 2:00–3:00 PM ET covering current research in hydrogeodesy and hydroseismology, data sharing in critical zone science, innovative technical tools, and building collaborations for hydrogeophysics.

title: Earth Science Information Partners (ESIP) Meeting · Events · CUAHSI
description: CUAHSI staff present the session Help Us, Help Ourselves: Sharing Infrastructure Across Repository Networks at 2:00 PM CT on July 29.

title: Call for Papers: Machine Learning for Water Resources (Frontiers in Water) · Events · CUAHSI
description: Submission deadline for the Frontiers in Water Research Topic "Improving Machine Learning for Water Resources through Scientific Knowledge Integration," edited by Dr. Jacob Zwart (USGS) and Dr. Xiaowei Jia (University of Pittsburgh).

title: HydroLearn Workshop and Hackathon · Events · CUAHSI
description: Annual HydroLearn workshop and hackathon for educators developing water science learning materials.

title: HydroLearn-CIROH 2026 Workshop and Hackathon · Events · CUAHSI
description: In-person workshop May 27–29 at the CIROH Developers Conference in Salt Lake City, followed by a virtual hackathon June 2–5 and June 8–11. Selected participants receive travel support. Participants work in pairs to create a peer-reviewed HydroLearn module with guidance from hydrology and education experts. HydroLearn already hosts 60+ peer-reviewed modules.

title: U.S. Indigenous Data Sovereignty & Governance Summit 2026 · Events · CUAHSI
description: Summit hosted by the U.S. Indigenous Data Sovereignty Network. Theme: "Coming Home: Indigenous Data Governance By Us For Us." Brings together Tribal and Indigenous leaders, community programs, scholars, and policy experts to advance Indigenous data governance. CUAHSI Fellow Kimmy Wong attended to better understand the data needs of Indigenous communities.

title: Leveraging HydroShare for Collaborative Research Data Management · Events · CUAHSI
description: Time: 2:00 to 4:30 pm ET. A 2.5-hour lecture-style webinar on how HydroShare supports the full research data lifecycle, from planning and collection through description, preservation, discovery and integration. Open to any researcher interested in using HydroShare, with no capacity limit.

title: Native American Fish and Wildlife Society National Conference · Events · CUAHSI
description: CUAHSI staff attending and presenting.

title: Navigating (beyond) Academic Waters: Navigating Today's Federal Job Market · Events · CUAHSI
description: Time: 1 to 2 pm ET. A session in the 2026 Navigating (beyond) Academic Waters series, hosted by the AGU Hydrology Section Student Subcommittee and CUAHSI for early career hydrologists. It brings together federal workers and contractors to discuss the current landscape and give a practical overview of today's federal job market. Good for graduate students weighing careers outside the tenure track. Speakers: Emily Smail (NOAA), Emil Cherrington (University of Notre Dame), Lauren N Schaefer (USGS) and Shih-Chieh Kao (Oak Ridge National Laboratory).

title: 2026 Near-Surface Geophysics Community Input Workshop · Events · CUAHSI
description: A two-day workshop bringing together the near-surface geophysics community to assess gaps and coordination opportunities and produce a community-informed Workshop Report. Sponsored by the NSF National Geophysical Facility (operated by EarthScope); jointly planned with CTEMPs, CUAHSI, NHERI, OpenTopography, and the AGU Near-Surface Geophysics Section. Travel support available for accepted attendees.

title: Introduction to NEON for Hydrology: Data Skills Demo · Events · CUAHSI
description: Data Skills Demo: Exploring the Water Cycle at Co-Located Terrestrial-Aquatic Sites. Join NEON data managers for a hands-on webinar walking participants through downloading and exploring various NEON hydrologic data products. Part of the Introduction to NEON for Hydrology cyberseminar series.

title: CUAHSI Skills Certificate Pilot: Reproducible Workflows with Open Water Data · Events · CUAHSI
description: A four-week, Python-based virtual course on programmatic access to NASA SWOT, NOAA National Water Model and USGS Water Data for the Nation data, developed with support from NASA, NOAA and USGS. About 20 hours, including 14 hours of live sessions, and a completion certificate for participants who pass the quizzes and give a final presentation. Intermediate Python experience is expected. The Fall 2026 pilot accepts 30 participants; registration closes October 23, 2026. A subset of the content is also presented in person at the Water Science Exchange on November 12 to 14. Members of CUAHSI member institutions receive a 20% discount.

title: Snow Measurement Field School 2026 · Events · CUAHSI
description: Hands-on field training in snow measurement methods at Snow Mountain Ranch. Curriculum progresses from snow pit fundamentals to student-designed mini field campaigns. Includes visits to a SNOTEL site and Fraser Experimental Forest.

title: Snow Measurement Field School 2027 · Events · CUAHSI
description: Hands-on, field-based training in snow measurement techniques, needed as ground truth for remotely sensed data, as input to hydrological and ecological models, and for avalanche forecasting. Open to graduate students, postdocs, professionals and senior scientists, modelers and remote sensors, with priority for graduate students and early career researchers. Participants must be able to spend days active in snow, and prior participants are not eligible. The final date to submit applications is October 7, 2026.

title: CUAHSI Spring Virtual Open House · Events · CUAHSI
description: CUAHSI's twice-yearly Virtual Open House — lightning-talk updates on HydroShare development, the CIROH Community Hydrofabric Project, data skill-building training, the Water Content Portal, and new engagement opportunities, followed by breakout discussions.

title: Universities Council on Water Resources Annual Conference · Events · CUAHSI
description: CUAHSI will exhibit and host a workshop: A Practical Overview of Publishing, Discovering, and Reusing Water Data with HydroShare.

title: UTA Summer Workshop on Water Resources Management · Events · CUAHSI
description: The University of Texas at Arlington summer workshop open to undergraduate students at any U.S. university. Covers water abundance, distribution, movement, governance, economic equity, and rights in the U.S. and globally. Live online sessions June 15–16; asynchronous component June 17–26. Applications due May 31.

title: CUAHSI Virtual Open House · Events · CUAHSI
description: Connect with CUAHSI staff, hear updates on upcoming plans, and learn where there's room to get more involved or share your perspectives. Staff-led updates and demos with opportunities for discussion and Q&A. Drop in or move between sessions as your schedule allows.

title: CUAHSI Virtual Open House · Events · CUAHSI
description: Time: 12 to 2 pm ET. Connect with CUAHSI staff, hear updates on upcoming plans, and share your perspectives. Brief updates on recent work and upcoming opportunities, plus group discussions on AI in the water sciences and CUAHSI's education resources for instructors. Agenda (ET): 12:00 welcome and event overview, CEO Jordan Read; 12:15 working with HydroShare data using the Python Client; 12:30 Hydrologic Knowledge Process Hub; 12:45 upcoming events and opportunities; 1:00 breakout discussions, either AI in the Water Sciences or For Instructors: Teaching with CUAHSI's Open Learning Resources.

title: Water Data Forum: Water Management for Data Centers · Events · CUAHSI
description: A panel discussion co-hosted by Cleveland Water Alliance, CUAHSI, and the Water Environment Federation examining water and wastewater considerations in data center operations. Panelists from Park Place Technologies, PNNL, and Virginia Tech; moderated by the Water Environment Federation.

title: Water Data Forum: Durable Skills for the Water Workforce in the Age of AI · Events · CUAHSI
description: Time: 12 to 1 pm ET. A free Water Data Forum webinar, held on Zoom, on durable skills for the water workforce in the age of AI, convened by Cleveland Water Alliance, the Water Environment Federation and CUAHSI. Panelists examine which analytical and modeling skills remain durable and what it means for hiring and for the water workforce. Speakers: Dr. Alison Appling (U.S. Geological Survey), John Ikeda (Water Environment Federation) and Ed Verhamme (Limnotech); CUAHSI CEO Jordan Read moderates.

title: Water Prediction Innovators Summer Institute · Events · CUAHSI
description: Seven-week experiential learning program bringing graduate students together with academic researchers and professionals to advance water prediction and flood forecasting in the United States. Students work in small teams, mentored by university faculty and other experts in the field. Supported by CIROH with NOAA funding (award NA22NWS4320003).

title: Water Science Exchange: Water in Working Landscapes · Events · CUAHSI
description: The first Water Science Exchange, a two-and-a-half day gathering at the University of Missouri that brings together water science researchers across career stages and institutions for skill-building workshops, a poster session, presentation opportunities and visits to local field sites. Students are especially encouraged to attend. Anyone affiliated with a CUAHSI member institution receives a 20% discount on registration. Early-bird registration runs through October 15 (extended from October 8) and registration closes October 29. Poster proposals are due October 21; posters are shown to up to 100 attendees. A special topics forum on AI in the water sciences is led by CUAHSI CEO Jordan Read. Field trips: the Central Mississippi River Basin Long-Term Agroecosystem Research (LTAR) site tour (USDA-ARS) and the Missouri Ozarks AmeriFlux (MOFLUX) site tour (University of Missouri and Oak Ridge National Laboratory). A limited number of travel stipends are available, first come, first served, with preference for students and postdocs presenting a poster; request one when registering. The hotel room block deadline is October 15.

title: Water Science Exchange: Early-Bird Registration Deadline · Events · CUAHSI
description: Last day of early-bird registration for the Water Science Exchange: Water in Working Landscapes (November 12 to 14, 2026), extended from October 8 to October 15. Early-bird rates, from September 10 to October 15: student member $110, student non-member $145, professional member $250, professional non-member $320. Anyone affiliated with a CUAHSI member institution receives a 20% discount.

title: Water Science Exchange: General Registration Deadline · Events · CUAHSI
description: Last day of general registration for the Water Science Exchange: Water in Working Landscapes (November 12 to 14, 2026). General rates, after early-bird registration ends on October 15 and through October 29: student member $140, student non-member $175, professional member $280, professional non-member $350. Anyone affiliated with a CUAHSI member institution receives a 20% discount.

title: WaterSoftHack 2026 · Events · CUAHSI
description: Cyberinfrastructure and Machine Learning Training to Advance Water Science Research. Collaborative effort led by Dr. Vidya Samadi (Clemson University) with the University of Iowa, Tulane University, and CUAHSI. This year focuses on cloud and edge computing. Participants gain hands-on experience running machine learning models in cloud and edge computing environments. Graduate and undergraduate students, postdocs, engineers, professionals, and early-career faculty are encouraged to apply.

title: WaterSoftHack 2026 · Events · CUAHSI
description: Led by Dr. Vidya Samadi (Clemson University) with University of Iowa, Tulane University, and CUAHSI. This year's focus is cloud and edge computing, equipping participants with hands-on experience running machine learning models in cloud and edge computing environments.

title: Women Advancing River Research: Bedrock Water Storage, Forest Health, and Streamflow · Events · CUAHSI

title: Women Advancing River Research: Hydroclimate Impacts on Human-Water Interactions · Events · CUAHSI
